items.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I have a brother who is a pianist who is also in New York and worked briefly with Miles years ago.

ctx.x: Yeah. You are an outstanding bass player. And you’ve been on just a scad of recordings. But how did you get started? First of all what attracted you to the bass as to other instruments.

I’m really a percussionist. I started out wanting to be a concert percussionist. I was not really interested in jazz at all but I wanted to be a classical percussionist. But my father was a drummer who grew up with Count Basie, grew up in Kansas City, so he goes back to the Count Basie early days, and I have a brother who is a pianist who is also in New York and worked briefly with Miles years ago. And I have a brother who is a vibist. So since my father was also a drummer, I figured there was no reason for me to…

playing football, but what about your hands? What if something happens to your hands? And eventually he won out. I finally really got serious about the string bass and I studied with a teacher at Northwestern University. I’m from Evanston, Illinois, so I spent a lot of time at Northwestern. And I graduated from Roosevelt University in Chicago in Musical Therapy. But I’ve been working as a musician for years and never really gotten into the musical therapy, but that’s kind of how I got around to the string bass.…
